title: Topology of rational points of quasi-separated algebraic spaces
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $Z$ an algebraic space over $K$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] whose diagonal $Z\to Z\times_K Z$ is quasi-compact. This means that after every scheme test the inverse image of each quasi-compact open subset is quasi-compact. Use the atlas topology and field-valued point convention of [lem-sfb-smooth-presentation-closed-subsets], applied to algebraic spaces as stacks with trivial automorphisms. Then the map $Z(K)\to|Z|$ sending a $K$-morphism $\operatorname{Spec}K\to Z$ to its underlying point is injective, and the image of each such morphism is a closed singleton. No finite-type, reducedness or separatedness hypothesis is imposed on $Z$.

source.place: Tag 03JX (lemma-bounded-fibres), quasi-separated implies decent; Tag 07U5 (lemma-algebraic-residue-field-extension-closed-point) with S=Spec K and k=K; Tag 0H1T (lemma-factor-through-residual-space-decent) and Tag 0H1R (lemma-residual-space-monomorphism) for the field-valued representative and its uniqueness over K.

proof.text: Fix a $K$-point $a:\operatorname{Spec}K\to Z$ and let $x$ be its point class. Apply [lem-sfb-qs-space-field-monomorphism] over $S=\operatorname{Spec}K$: the assumed relative diagonal is quasi-compact, so choose a quasi-compact monomorphism $j:\operatorname{Spec}F\to Z$ representing $x$. Give $\operatorname{Spec}F$ the induced map to $\operatorname{Spec}K$. By [def-weil-affine-spectrum] this is a field homomorphism $i:K\to F$. The point classes of [lem-sfb-smooth-presentation-closed-subsets] and of [def-a1-space-point-topology] are the same: field-valued maps identified after restriction to a common extension field. So $x\in|Z|$ in the sense of the cited lemma.

The field spectrum $\operatorname{Spec}K$ is reduced, since a field has no nonzero nilpotents. Apply [lem-sfb-reduced-singleton-field-factorization] to $a$ and $j$ to obtain $g:\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ over $K$ with $j\circ g=a$. By [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $g$ corresponds to a field homomorphism $h:F\to K$ satisfying $h\circ i=\mathrm{id}_K$. If $b$ is a second $K$-point with the same point class $x$, the same lemma factors it through this same $j$, giving $h':F\to K$ with $h'\circ i=\mathrm{id}_K$.

source.place: Tags 0H1T (lemma-factor-through-residual-space-decent) and 0H1R (lemma-residual-space-monomorphism); uniqueness follows from the monomorphism hypothesis.

proof.text: A unital homomorphism from a field has zero kernel: a nonzero kernel element would have an inverse and force $1=0$. Thus $h$ is injective. For $u\in F$, $h(i(h(u)))=h(u)$, so injectivity gives $i(h(u))=u$. Therefore $i$ is surjective and $h$ is its inverse. For every $u=i(v)$ we also have $h'(u)=v=h(u)$, so $h'=h$. The uniqueness of the ring map corresponding to an affine-scheme morphism in [def-weil-affine-spectrum] gives equality of the two factorizations and hence $b=a$. This proves injectivity of $Z(K)\to|Z|$.

source.place: Elementary field retraction argument after the factorization of Tag 0H1T.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-qs-space-field-monomorphism], every point of $Z$ has a quasi-compact field monomorphism representative, which is precisely the hypothesis on $X$ in [lem-sfb-decent-algebraic-field-image-closed]. Apply that lemma with $S=\operatorname{Spec}K$, $X=Z$, $L=K$, and the given $a$. By [def-weil-affine-spectrum] the base has one point with residue field $K$; its singleton is the whole space and is closed. The induced field extension is the identity $K\to K$, algebraic because $u\in K$ satisfies $T-u$. The lemma therefore makes the image of $a$ a closed singleton for the topology of [def-a1-space-point-topology], which for the algebraic space $Z$ is its usual atlas topology, the quotient topology from a surjective etale scheme atlas $U\to Z$. An etale morphism is smooth (of relative dimension zero) by [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], so $U\to Z$ is a smooth surjective scheme atlas, and [lem-sfb-smooth-presentation-closed-subsets] makes the quotient topology independent of the smooth atlas. Hence the image of $a$ is a closed singleton also in the topology fixed in the statement. The case $Z(K)=\varnothing$ is vacuous. No property of $Z$ beyond its stated diagonal hypothesis was used.

lean.statement: theorem qsSpace_rationalPoint_topology (K : Type u) [Field K] (Z : AlgebraicSpace (Spec (.of K))) (hdiag : IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ QuasiCompact p.left) (prod.lift (𝟙 Z.obj.obj) (𝟙 Z.obj.obj))) : Function.Injective (rationalPointClass K Z) ∧ ∀ a : yoneda.obj (Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec (.of K)))) ⟶ Z.obj.obj, @IsClosed _ (moduliSmoothPointTopology (discreteModuli Z.obj.obj)) {rationalPointClass K Z a}
lean.note: Uses ModuliPoints and moduliSmoothPointTopology on the existing discreteModuli of the algebraic space, as required by the recorded smooth-presentation dependency. rationalPointClass is the concrete class of the specified natural transformation from Spec K; no auxiliary point quotient or topology is introduced. The diagonal hypothesis uses IsRepresentableWith QuasiCompact on the relative product diagonal.
